items.title: Rural Health Network Development Planning Program
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: access to care, underserved communities; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: The Rural Health Network Development Planning Program funds the planning and development of rural integrated health care networks focused on collaboration among entities to improve local capacity and care coordination in underserved rural communities. It aims to help these networks expand access, improve quality of care, and strengthen the rural health care system. The program supports efforts to increase health information technology use and explore alternative health care delivery models.
items.why_it_fits: This grant supports strengthening rural health care systems and improving rural health delivery, aligning with the main agency goal to modernize programs for a sustainable rural health delivery system.

items.title: Rural Health Value Program
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: rural health, value-based care; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: The Rural Health Value (RHV) Program funds one recipient to provide analysis and technical assistance to rural stakeholders. The goal is to help rural providers understand and engage in value-based care payment and delivery models to improve their participation and success. This funding focuses specifically on rural health care providers.
items.why_it_fits: This grant supports the main agency goal by promoting value-based care and strengthening rural health delivery systems.
items.eligibility_note: One recipient is funded; specific eligible applicants are not stated.
items.risk_note: Only one recipient will be funded, which may increase competition and risk of not receiving the grant.

items.title: Rural Health Network Development Program
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: rural health, rural hospitals; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: The Rural Health Network Development Program funds integrated health care networks that serve targeted rural communities. It offers two funding tracts: one to support established networks of independent rural hospitals and clinics to improve operations and services, and another to assist early-stage rural health networks in planning and expanding clinical or operational services. The program aims to expand access, improve care coordination and quality, and strengthen rural health systems.
items.why_it_fits: This grant supports rural health delivery by strengthening rural health networks and improving access and efficiency, aligning with the goal to modernize and sustain rural health care systems.
items.eligibility_note: Applicants include integrated rural health care networks, specifically independent rural hospitals and clinics or nascent/early-stage rural health care networks.
items.risk_note: Applicants must address small scale structural barriers and demonstrate ability to collaborate in integrated networks, which may be challenging for small rural providers.

items.title: Appalachian Region Healthcare Support Program
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: rural health, rural hospitals; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: The Appalachian Region Healthcare Support Program provides technical assistance to rural healthcare organizations, including critical access hospitals, small rural hospitals, rural health clinics, and tribal healthcare facilities in the Appalachian Region. The program aims to strengthen healthcare delivery by improving financial and operational performance and the quality of care in these rural organizations.
items.why_it_fits: This grant supports the main goal by strengthening rural health delivery systems and improving healthcare operations in state-served rural areas.
items.eligibility_note: Rural healthcare organizations located in the rural counties served by the Appalachian Regional Commission, including critical access hospitals, small rural hospitals, rural health clinics, and tribal healthcare facilities.

items.title: Centers of Excellence in Healthcare Quality and Safety
items.reason: Closest goal: G5 (Organizational excellence); matched terms: rural hospitals; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: This grant funds the creation of a collaborative network of healthcare systems, facilities, and public health partners to detect, respond to, and prevent threats to patient and healthcare worker safety. It supports improving the safety, quality, and resilience of healthcare delivery across various healthcare settings including hospitals, nursing homes, dialysis centers, emergency rooms, outpatient facilities, and home health providers.
items.why_it_fits: The grant supports organizational excellence by fostering collaboration and improving healthcare quality and safety, aligning with goals of data-driven decision making and public health infrastructure.
items.eligibility_note: Healthcare systems inclusive of multiple facilities in a variety of settings, partnering with public health departments and other relevant entities, can apply; however, each applicant is not expected to have all elements.
items.risk_note: Applicants must establish and maintain a collaborative network across diverse healthcare settings and public health partners, which may be complex and resource-intensive.

items.title: The National Rural Health Information Technology Assessment Program
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: rural health; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: This grant funds efforts to help rural communities address challenges and gaps in using health information technology to improve health and wellness. It is aimed at supporting rural areas in leveraging IT for better health outcomes. The program focuses on enhancing health information technology capabilities in rural settings.
items.why_it_fits: This grant supports the main goal by addressing rural health delivery through improving health information technology in rural communities.

items.title: Rural Communities Opioid Response Program - Child and Adolescent Behavioral Health
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: mental health, substance use disorder; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: This grant funds rural communities to establish and expand behavioral health care services focused on mental health and substance use disorder for rural children and adolescents. It aims to improve access to these critical services in rural areas. The program targets child and adolescent behavioral health needs in rural settings.
items.why_it_fits: This grant supports the main goal by enhancing rural health delivery through expanding behavioral health services in rural communities.

items.title: Rural Residency Planning and Development Program
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: Medicaid; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: The Rural Residency Planning and Development Program provides start-up funding to create new, accredited rural physician residency programs in qualifying specialties to increase training and practice in rural areas. It targets rural residency programs that train physicians for rural communities to address physician shortages. The program supports specialties including family medicine, internal medicine, psychiatry, general surgery, and obstetrics and gynecology.
items.why_it_fits: This grant fits the main goal by supporting rural health delivery through the development of sustainable rural residency programs that increase physician availability in rural areas.
items.eligibility_note: Accredited physician residency programs that train residents in clinical training sites physically located in a rural area as defined by HRSA's Federal Office of Rural Health Policy for more than 50 percent of residency time.
items.risk_note: Long-term sustainability funding must come from viable and stable sources such as Medicare, Medicaid, or other public or private sources, which may pose a funding risk.

items.reason: Closest goal: G4 (Sustainable workforce); matched terms: health workforce; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: The Health Workforce Research Centers fund research to help decision-makers at federal, state, and local levels understand health workforce needs. The grant supports activities that generate data and insights about the health workforce.
items.why_it_fits: This grant supports understanding health workforce needs, which aligns with developing and improving the medical workforce under the main agency goal.

items.title: Children's Mental Health Initiative

items.why_it_fits: This grant supports the main goal by improving access to mental health care for children and youth, addressing a key medical need through care coordination.

items.title: Rural Maternity and Obstetrics Management Strategies Program
items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); funder usually supports this mission.

items.why_it_fits: This grant supports improving rural health delivery, aligning with the main goal to modernize and sustain rural health care systems.

items.title: NIOSH Centers of Excellence for Total Worker Health® (U19)
items.agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention - ERA
items.reason: Closest goal: G5 (Organizational excellence); matched terms: mental health, substance use disorder; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: This grant funds Centers of Excellence in Total Worker Health® to conduct rigorous research and translation activities aimed at preventing harmful exposures, improving working conditions, and advancing worker well-being. items.reason: Closest goal: G3 (Transform and modernize health care); matched terms: value-based care; funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: This grant funds State and Regional Primary Care Associations (PCAs) to provide technical assistance that supports health centers and look-alikes in delivering high-quality preventive and primary health care services. It aims to improve access, chronic disease management, workforce development, emergency preparedness, value-based care implementation, and data-driven improvements in health centers.
items.why_it_fits: The grant supports implementing value-based care delivery and improving health care operations, aligning with the main goal to transform and modernize health care delivery.
items.eligibility_note: State and Regional Primary Care Associations (PCAs) that support Health Center Program award recipients and look-alikes.
items.risk_note: Applicants must be able to deliver technical assistance across multiple areas including workforce training, emergency preparedness, and value-based care implementation, which may require diverse expertise and coordination.

items.title: Promoting Access with a Language Services Assistance Symbol
items.agency: Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health
items.reason: Closest goal: G1 (Access to care); funder usually supports this mission.
items.summary: This grant funds demonstration projects to support and evaluate the use of a universal symbol indicating the availability of language assistance services in health settings, aimed at improving healthcare access for individuals with limited English proficiency and communication disabilities. Eligible applicants include private nonprofit or public entities located in a State, including faith-based and community-based organizations. items.risk_note: Applicants must have active SAM.gov registration and submit applications through Grants.gov, which may require early preparation and coordination.
